questions.0.explain.t: SCA (software composition analysis) inventories what you import and cross-references it with vulnerability databases.

questions.0.options.0.t: Logic errors in the code written by the team itself

questions.0.options.1.t: Third-party dependencies, their versions, CVEs and licenses

questions.0.options.2.t: The coverage of the automated tests of each module

questions.0.options.3.t: The CPU and memory use of the containers in production

questions.1.explain.t: Most CVEs in real projects come from transitive dependencies that nobody declared directly.

questions.1.options.0.t: An optional dependency used only during development

questions.1.options.1.t: A dependency brought in indirectly by another one you declared

questions.1.options.2.t: A dependency copied by hand into the repository

questions.1.options.3.t: A dependency that declares no usage license

questions.2.explain.t: The code can stand still while a new CVE hits a dependency you already use.

questions.2.options.0.t: Because new CVEs are published after deploy, against code that did not change

questions.2.options.1.t: Because the build changes the dependency versions by itself on every run

questions.2.options.2.t: Because the SCA result expires every 24 hours and has to be renewed

questions.2.options.3.t: Because the pipeline deletes the previous results when it finishes

questions.2.q.t: Why does SCA need to run continuously and not only at build?
